title: Who was Robert Maxwell?
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck profile Robert Maxwell (born Jan Ludwig Hoch in Slatvinne, Czechoslovakia, 1923), a British media tycoon, war hero, Labour MP and fraudster. They cover his escape from the Nazis, wartime service with the British Army and MI6, founding Pergamon Press and scientific publishing, his newspaper rivalry with Rupert Murdoch, his parliamentary career and bullying reputation, his family life including daughter Ghislaine, the pension fund scandal and collapse of his empire, and the mysterious 1991 yacht death (accident, suicide, or murder theories), followed by listener mail about tobacco settlement payments in Minnesota.

segments.title: Opening and Great Man theory
segments.summary: Hosts introduce Robert Maxwell as a notoriously awful but accomplished figure and explain the great man view of history.

segments.title: Childhood and escape from the Nazis
segments.summary: Maxwell's poor childhood in Czechoslovakia, his Jewish background, his escape from the Nazi takeover in 1939, and his arrest and escape while working with the Hungarian and Czech resistance.

segments.title: British Army service and intelligence work
segments.summary: Maxwell joins the Foreign Legion, then the British Army, earns a Military Cross, is accused of war crimes that could not be corroborated, and is recruited by MI6 after speaking many languages.

segments.title: Postwar Berlin and business opportunities
segments.summary: Maxwell's postwar work in Berlin interviewing German prisoners and profiting from the devastated European real estate market, leading him into publishing.

segments.title: Pergamon Press and German scientific books
segments.summary: Maxwell learns of stockpiled German scientific books and journals at Springer Verlag, partners with Paul Rosebaud to form Pergamon Press, and gets MI6 financing to ship about 300 tons of books to London.

segments.title: Simpkin Marshall and private equity comparison
segments.summary: Maxwell buys Simpkin Marshall with a loan, then guts it by borrowing against its credit and selling assets, which the hosts compare to private equity raiding companies.

segments.title: Business reputation and rivalry with Rupert Murdoch
segments.summary: Maxwell's reputation for not repaying debts and Springer's break with him, the Board of Trade declaring him unfit to run a public company, and his obsessive newspaper-buying rivalry with Rupert Murdoch, including the Daily Mirror purchase.

segments.title: Expansion spending spree and Tetris loss
segments.summary: Maxwell's US and European expansion, including McGraw-Hill and the New York Daily News purchase, which overextended his empire, and the loss of Tetris rights through Mirrorsoft.

segments.title: Parliament career
segments.summary: Maxwell becomes a Labour MP from 1964 to 1970 despite conservative leanings, is disliked by colleagues, and is arrested for driving while shaving.

segments.title: Bullying behavior and family life
segments.summary: Accounts of Maxwell's bullying of staff, his mansion Headington Hill Hall, his treatment of his children, and his wife Betty's six rules for marriage.

segments.title: Children, favoritism and estate
segments.summary: Maxwell's children, including the deaths of daughter Karine and son Michael, his favoritism toward Ghislaine, and his decision to leave his estate only to his sons.

segments.title: Financial collapse and pension fund raiding
segments.summary: Maxwell's final months on the yacht Lady Ghislaine, the diversion of close to 500 million pounds from pension funds, share buying to prop up prices, and creditors calling in debts.

segments.title: Spy allegations and Vanunu
segments.summary: Maxwell's paranoia and bugging, allegations he spied for Israel, the Vanunu nuclear story he allegedly stalled, and Seymour Hersh's reporting and the parliamentary debate.

segments.title: Death at sea and theories
segments.summary: Maxwell's fall from the Lady Ghislaine in November 1991, the pathologists' disagreement, and accident, suicide, murder, and faked-death theories, plus the aftermath for his family and the pensioners.

segments.title: Family legacy and show notes
segments.summary: Hosts discuss the Maxwell family's reputational damage and point listeners to further resources, including a BBC documentary.

segments.title: Listener mail on tobacco settlements
segments.summary: Listener Jeremiah Wingstedt clarifies how Minnesota's tobacco settlement payments work, including annual payments and the six point five billion estimate.
